Title: Best day to gather in person
Detail_lesson: Teams that meet in person some of the time rarely agree on which day earns the travel.
CustomInstruction: Answer with one weekday and a reason of five words or fewer. Pick the reason you would actually defend out loud.

Title: Meetings you can absorb in a day
Detail_lesson: There is a number above which meetings stop being coordination and start being the work itself.
CustomInstruction: Give a number, then name the type of meeting that breaks the limit first for you.

Title: Core hours worth protecting
Detail_lesson: Distributed teams trade overlap for flexibility, and the right balance is genuinely contested.
CustomInstruction: Answer with a number of hours per day, assuming colleagues several time zones away. Say what you would protect those hours for.

Title: Fastest way to reach you
Detail_lesson: Everyone has a preferred channel and a channel they actually check. They are often not the same.
CustomInstruction: Name a single channel and the response time you would realistically hit on it. Do not list a backup.

Title: Camera on or camera off
Detail_lesson: Video defaults get set once, early, and are rarely revisited even as teams change shape.
CustomInstruction: Take a side in three words. Then give the one situation where you would do the opposite.

Title: How often a status update is worth writing
Detail_lesson: Update cadence is usually inherited rather than chosen, and often serves a reader nobody has identified.
CustomInstruction: Give a frequency, then say who the update is genuinely for: the team, a manager, or you.

Title: Learn by doing or read first
Detail_lesson: Most people have a strong default and assume it is the universal one.
CustomInstruction: Pick one and name the last thing you learned that way. One sentence, with the actual thing named.

Title: The right length for a training session
Detail_lesson: Attention, retention and calendar reality pull in different directions here.
CustomInstruction: Answer with a duration and the format that duration needs: talk, workshop, or self-paced.

Title: One tool you would remove
Detail_lesson: Tool sprawl is easy to complain about and hard to reverse, because every tool has at least one committed user.
CustomInstruction: Name a single tool and what takes over its job. If nothing replaces it, say what simply stops happening.

Title: Written doc or short video
Detail_lesson: The same explanation lands very differently depending on the medium and the reader's hurry.
CustomInstruction: Choose one for explaining a process to a colleague. Then name the situation that flips your answer.
